findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: An employee was observed to wash their hands and then not utilize a barrier to shut off the faucet, thus recontaminating their hands. This employee was educated on site about the importance of a barrier when handling the faucet to not recontaminate hands. Ensure employees are educated and trained on proepr hand washing techniques. 
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: At the start of the inspection there was a single sanitizer bucket observed made up with apparent soap film on top. The solution was tested and recorded at 0ppm chlorine. All other sanitizer buckets were observed dumped and not available. A new sanitizer bucket was created and tested at 100ppm chlorine. Ensure test strips are regularly used to ensure the efficacy of the sanitizer remains intact and ensure sanitizer buckets are readily available during all hours of operation. 
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on device and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

(C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: The walk-in cooler is observed still in disrepair during today’s spot check. For a temporary solution, a double door cooler has been placed in the main lobby area of the kitchen to allow for adequate cold holding space. An additional follow-up is being scheduled for February 7, 2024. 
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: The walk-in cooler was observed operating at 51 degrees F during today’s inspection. PIC informed the inspector the walk-in cooler was down as of this morning. PIC and inspector temped items and determined the following items were not salvageable and the following items were voluntarily discarded during today’s inspection: All pre-cut lettuce bagged and prepped, Pea Salad, Individual Salad Cups, Baby Carrots, Anytime Snack Packs, Opened container of Ranch, Opened container of Mayo, Baked Potatoes, and prepackaged boiled eggs. 
Service calls have been made to have the cooler repaired, please see General Comments for additional details. Temperatures are taken of the cooler each morning and shall continue to be taken routinely each day to ensure proper cold holding temperatures of 41 degrees F or below.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: There was observed a box of boiled eggs prepackaged and stored in the walk-in cooler. The eggs, out of temp, see violation #22, were observed with a best by date of 12-13-2023 and were voluntarily discarded during today’s inspection. Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date. Ensure that food items are discarded if they exceed the use by date set by the manufacturer.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment: Observed chicken strips in the reach in cooler (and a smaller batch in the prep cooler) that were reported to have been removed from cooking around 6:30 am and were observed wrapped (with condensation) and probed at 68F. Cooling logs are not available and it is unknown at what time chicken reached 70F, but it appears as though this did not occur in 2 hours since at almost 4 hours later it is 68F. Chicken strips were voluntarily discarded. Cooling methods for this type of item need to be discussed so that cooling can occur rapidly and food cool from 135F to 70F within 2 hours and to 41F or below within an additional 4 hours.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.15  (C) The method of cooling chicken is inadequate. Food must be uncovered during cooling, if protected from overhead contamination. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.citation_text: 750.1160 - Intact roach egg case was observed on a glue trap between the fryers and ovens. Egg case was shown to Kitchen Manager. Glue trap was folded to squish egg case, and trap was placed in a sealed plastic bag in the garbage for disposal. No other intact egg cases were observed, and no live roaches were observed. Contact PCO for service prior to spot check. Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. (see general comments)

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) Floor tiles below dish machine are damaged - a gap was observed in one area where the tile is warped from water damage. Replace all damaged tiles (cracked, gaps, etc.) below/around the dish machine. B) Floors were soiled along the walls/in corners under the dirty tray window by dish machine (glue trap w/ hatched roach egg case, roaches, and debris), behind ovens across from 3 part sink, and below dish machine (water and lime buildup around drain). Clean the floors throughout daily/as needed. (see general comments)

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Cheese sauce in warmer was 123F. Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135F/above after reaching proper cooking temperature. Cheese sauce was made earlier this morning. Employee placed sauce in the steamer to reheat product.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - Inside fryers (back ledges/sides) and side of oven by fryers were soiled. Clean inside the fryers and the side of the oven as needed to eliminate buildup of grease, food, and dust.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.citation_text: 750.1170 - (R) Door sweep to kitchen screen door was in disrepair - gaps w/ visible light were observed along the bottom. Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects. The outer door was closed during the inspection. **The outer door must be kept closed until the screen door is properly repaired. The inspector's pen fit through the opening at the bottom. If a mouse can fit its head through an opening it can get its body through. This is a potential entry point for mice & other pests. Do not prop open the door until the screen door is fixed** Work order has been placed and the screen door is scheduled for repair.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text: 750.530 - Employee was observed chewing gum while slicing tomatoes. Employees shall consume food (including candy & chewing gum) only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection. Employee discarded her gum in the trash during the inspection.
